title: Field-Free Reconfigurable Spin Logic in Compositionally Graded MnxCoAl Layer
authors: Haohang Cheng, Pengju Wang, Hongrui Qin, Rongkun Han, Dong Pan, Dahai Wei, Jianhua Zhao
abstract: Spintronic logic-in-memory provides a route to reducing data-transfer energy consumption and accelerating computation by integrating nonvolatile storage and logic functions within a single physical unit. Here, we investigate field-free spin-orbit-torque (SOT) switching and reconfigurable spin logic in a vertically composition-graded MnxCoAl/Pt heterostructure. In contrast to the uniform-composition Mn1.8CoAl/Pt and Mn2.5CoAl/Pt control devices, the Mn1.8-2.5CoAl gradient device exhibits deterministic SOT switching under zero external magnetic field. Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI)-related measurements reveal a finite characteristic effective-field scale, indicating the involvement of chiral magnetization-reversal processes. Meanwhile, the vertical composition gradient introduces magnetic inhomogeneity that can modify domain nucleation and propagation, and the combined effects are consistent with the observed field-free switching behavior. The composition-gradient device further exhibits accumulative multistate switching with stable intermediate Hall-resistance states under zero magnetic field, whereas the uniform-composition controls do not show comparable stable multistate behavior. By tailoring the amplitude, polarity, and sequence of current pulses, the device can be tuned between binary and multilevel switching modes, enabling the experimental realization of AND, OR, NAND, and NOR Boolean operations within the same Hall-bar device without any external magnetic field. These results extend Mn-Co-Al Heusler heterostructures from field-assisted SOT switching toward field-free magnetization control, multistate operation, and reconfigurable spin logic through vertical composition engineering.
summary: This work demonstrates a breakthrough in spintronics by utilizing a vertically composition-graded $	ext{Mn-Co-Al}$ Heusler heterostructure to achieve field-free magnetization control. The gradient structure enables stable, accumulative multistate switching, allowing the device to function as a reconfigurable logic element capable of performing all fundamental Boolean operations (AND, OR, NAND, NOR) purely electrically.
main_problem: The goal is to develop field-free, reconfigurable spin logic by integrating nonvolatile storage and logic functions into a single physical unit to reduce data-transfer energy consumption.
main_result: The compositionally graded $	ext{Mn}_x	ext{CoAl}/	ext{Pt}$ heterostructure successfully demonstrates deterministic field-free SOT switching, accumulative multistate switching, and the experimental realization of all four basic Boolean logic gates (AND, OR, NAND, NOR) at zero external magnetic field.
method: The research involves fabricating and characterizing vertically composition-graded magnetic films using MBE, followed by electrical transport measurements using current pulses to induce and read out magnetization states.
model_or_system: The physical system is a $	ext{Mn}_x	ext{CoAl}/	ext{Pt}$ Heusler heterostructure where the $	ext{Mn}$ content is varied vertically across the film. This gradient introduces magnetic inhomogeneity, which, combined with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI), enables novel magnetic switching behavior.
key_observables: Hall resistance ($	ext{R}_{xy}$) used to read logic states (positive/negative), saturation magnetization ($	ext{M}_s$), effective anisotropy field ($	ext{H}_k$), and the ability to perform logic operations (AND, OR, NAND, NOR).
important_parameters: Zero external magnetic field, current pulse amplitude/polarity (used to tune between binary and multilevel switching), and the composition gradient itself ($	ext{Mn}_{1.8-2.5}	ext{CoAl}$).
main_assumptions: The field-free switching and multistate behavior are attributed to the cooperative effects of DMI-related chiral reversal and the magnetic inhomogeneity induced by the vertical composition gradient.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structure (gradient), magnetic hysteresis loops, anomalous Hall effect curves, and detailed pulse protocols demonstrating the switching sequence required to implement the four Boolean logic gates.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for energy-efficient logic, characterizing the magnetic properties of the gradient structure versus uniform controls, demonstrating field-free SOT switching and multistate memory, and finally realizing the full set of Boolean logic operations using tailored current pulses.
why_interesting: While the core physics is in condensed matter spintronics, the concept of using engineered material gradients to induce complex, non-linear, and programmable switching behavior is relevant to understanding emergent phenomena in complex quantum or many-body systems.

(d) AHE resistance (Rxy) curves measured under a perpendicular magnetic field Hz. (e) Comparison of Ms, Hk, and Ku on the Mn composition x.

Figure 1(e) summarizes the saturation magnetization Ms, effective anisotropy field Hk, and magnetic anisotropy constant Ku of the three MnxCoAl samples. For the two uniform-composition samples, Ms decreases while Hk increases as the Mn content increases from x=1.8 to x=2.5. The Mn1.8-2.5CoAl gradient sample exhibits intermediate Ms and Hk values between those of Mn1.8CoAl and Mn2.5CoAl, consistent with its intermediate magnetic characteristics observed in the hysteresis measurements.
